evidence.note: AON6500 is DFN-8 3x3; Si4442DY is SO-8. Both 8-pin but different outline and land pattern. DFN is much smaller; Si4442DY will not fit a DFN footprint.
Both follow classic SO-8/DFN-8 N-channel pinout: pins 1-3 source, pin 4 gate, pins 5-8 drain.

CRITICAL: AON6500 RDS_on=12 mOhm at VGS=4.5V (logic-level); Si4442DY RDS_on=7.5 mOhm but specified at VGS=10V only. Si4442DY is NOT guaranteed logic-level — driving its gate from 5V will not fully enhance it and RDS_on will rise sharply.
AON6500 is logic-level (specified at VGS=4.5V). Si4442DY is standard-level (specified at VGS=10V). If the controller gate drive is 5V, Si4442DY is unsuitable.
AON6500 Qg=6 nC; Si4442DY Qg=14 nC — Si4442DY will switch slower and dissipate more gate-drive power.
Both Rtheta_ja=50 C/W class. Si4442DY Rtheta_jc=15 vs AON6500 8 C/W.

conditions: Footprint must be SO-8 on the board (not DFN-8).
Gate drive from the controller must be >=10V (NOT 5V). If driven from 5V, do NOT substitute.
Verify that the higher Qg of Si4442DY (14 nC vs 6 nC) does not exceed the controller's gate-drive capability at the switching frequency.
verification_notes: Electrically close in VDS/ID but critical difference in gate-drive level. CONDITIONAL only when board footprint and gate drive both permit.
